title: Pure and Mixed States, Ensembles, and Schmidt Decomposition

items.title: Density operator
items.statement:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root library's convention that the inner product is linear in its first argument. A **density operator** on $H$ is a non-negative endomorphism $\rho:H\to H$ with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho)=1$; non-negative and trace have the meanings of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]] and [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. The zero-dimensional space is excluded: its only endomorphism has trace $0$.

Here $\ker\rho=\{x\in H:\rho x=0\}$, using the kernel of a linear map from [[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]. The **support** of $\rho$ is the orthogonal complement of its kernel in the root convention:

$$\operatorname{supp}(\rho):=\{x\in H: \langle x,y\rangle=0\text{ for every }y\in\ker\rho\}.$$

For a subspace $S\subseteq H$, $\rho$ is **faithful on $S$** when $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)=S$ and the restriction $\rho|_S:S\to S$ is positive definite in the sense of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]. This restriction is an endomorphism: if $x\in S$ and $y\in\ker\rho$, self-adjointness gives $\langle\rho x,y\rangle=\langle x,\rho y\rangle=0$, so $\rho x\in(\ker\rho)^\perp=S$.

items.title: Finite positive effect family
items.statement: Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, and let $I_H:H\to H$ denote the identity map $x\mapsto x$. An **effect** on $H$ is an endomorphism $E$ such that both $E$ and $I_H-E$ are non-negative in the sense of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]. A **finite complete positive family** is a nonempty finite list $(E_1,\ldots,E_n)$ of non-negative endomorphisms with $\sum_{a=1}^n E_a=I_H$. The next lemma proves that every member of such a family is an effect, so the family is a finite complete effect family. This is algebraic data only; it does not assert a measurement law.

items.title: Pure state and ray
items.statement: Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. Two nonzero vectors $x,y\in H$ represent the same **ray** when $y=\alpha x$ for some nonzero $\alpha\in\mathbb C$. A **pure state** is such a ray. If $u$ is a unit representative, its associated operator is $P_u=|u\rangle\langle u|$, with the bra, ket and outer-product convention of [[def-qc-dirac-notation-conversion]]. The theorem [[thm-qc-ray-projector-well-defined-and-bijective]] proves that this operator is a rank-one orthogonal projection independent of the chosen unit representative, so it is the operator representative of the pure state.

items.title: A complete positive family consists of effects
items.statement: For a nonzero finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space $H$, if $E_1,\ldots,E_n$ is a finite complete positive family as defined in [[def-qc-finite-positive-effect-family]], then each $E_a$ is an effect: $E_a$ and $I_H-E_a$ are non-negative.

items.title: Every nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space admits a density operator
items.statement: Every nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $H$ admits a density operator; specifically, if $d=\dim_{\mathbb C}H$, then $I_H/d$ is a density operator on $H$.

items.title: Ray-to-projector is well-defined and bijective
items.statement: For nonzero finite-dimensional complex-inner-product $H$, the map sending a ray $[u]$ to the rank-one projector $P_u=|u\rangle\langle u|$ of any unit representative is well-defined and bijective onto the rank-one orthogonal projections on $H$. Each $P_u$ is non-negative and has trace one.

items.title: Schmidt decomposition
items.statement:
Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex-inner-product spaces with the tensor-product convention of [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]. For every $\Psi\in H\otimes K$ there are an integer $r\ge0$, positive numbers $s_1,\ldots,s_r$, and orthonormal families $u_1,\ldots,u_r\in H$ and $v_1,\ldots,v_r\in K$ such that

$$\Psi=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j u_j\otimes v_j,\qquad \|\Psi\|^2=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j^2.$$

For $\Psi=0$ take $r=0$ and the empty sum. For any chosen ordered pair of orthonormal bases, the construction below obtains the $s_j$ as the positive singular values of the coefficient matrix of $\Psi$ in their ordered product basis.

items.title: Ensemble and purification
items.statement:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space. A **finite ensemble of density operators** on $H$ is a positive integer $n$, weights $p_1,\ldots,p_n\ge0$ with $\sum_{a=1}^np_a=1$, and density operators $\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_n$ on $H$. Its **barycenter** is $\bar\rho=\sum_{a=1}^np_a\rho_a$. A zero-weight component still names a density operator but contributes zero to the barycenter.

Let $K$ be any finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space. A **purification** of a density operator $\rho$ on $H$ is a unit vector $\Psi\in H\otimes K$ such that

$$\operatorname{Tr}_K(|\Psi\rangle\langle\Psi|)=\rho.$$

The tensor factors are ordered $H$ then $K$. Tensor products, outer products and partial trace have the conventions of [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[def-qc-dirac-notation-conversion]] and [[def-qc-partial-trace]]. The auxiliary space may be any finite dimension that supports such a unit vector.

items.title: Density operators have an orthogonal spectral ensemble
items.statement:
Let $\rho$ be a density operator on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space $H$. Then there are $m=\operatorname{rank}(\rho)\ge1$, positive numbers $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m$ with $\sum_{j=1}^m\lambda_j=1$, and orthonormal unit vectors $e_1,\ldots,e_m$ such that

$$\rho=\sum_{j=1}^m\lambda_j|e_j\rangle\langle e_j|.$$

The eigenvectors with eigenvalue zero are omitted; the displayed pure-state projectors are pairwise orthogonal.

items.title: Finite ensemble barycenters are density operators
items.statement: For a finite ensemble $(p_a,\rho_a)_{a=1}^n$ of density operators on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space $H$, its barycenter $\bar\rho=\sum_{a=1}^np_a\rho_a$ is a density operator. Regrouping the finite outcomes into blocks and assigning each block its normalized barycenter when its total weight is positive preserves the overall barycenter; zero-total-weight blocks contribute zero.

items.title: Purifications exist and are unitarily equivalent after padding
items.statement:
Every density operator $\rho$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space $H$ has a purification on some finite-dimensional auxiliary space. More precisely, if $r=\operatorname{rank}(\rho)$, it has one on an auxiliary space of dimension $r$. If $\Psi_i\in H\otimes K_i$ ($i=1,2$) are any two purifications of the same $\rho$, then for every integer $m\ge\max(\dim K_1,\dim K_2)$ and every pair of linear isometric embeddings $\iota_i:K_i\to\mathbb C^m$, where $\mathbb C^m$ has its standard complex inner product, there is a unitary $U$ on $\mathbb C^m$ such that

$$ (I_H\otimes U)(I_H\otimes\iota_2)\Psi_2=(I_H\otimes\iota_1)\Psi_1. $$

items.title: Rank-one density operators are pure-state projectors
items.statement: Every pure-state ray projector on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space is a density operator. Conversely, every rank-one density operator is the projector of a unique pure-state ray.

items.title: Every finite state ensemble is obtainable from a purification
items.statement:
Let $(p_a,\sigma_a)_{a=1}^n$ be a finite ensemble of density operators on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space $H$, with barycenter $\rho=\sum_ap_a\sigma_a$. For every finite-dimensional auxiliary space $K$ and every purification $\Psi\in H\otimes K$ of $\rho$, there is a finite complete effect family $(E_a)_{a=1}^n$ on $K$ such that

$$\operatorname{Tr}_K\!\left[(I_H\otimes\sqrt{E_a})|\Psi\rangle\langle\Psi|(I_H\otimes\sqrt{E_a})\right]=p_a\sigma_a$$

for each $a$. In particular, for a pure-state ensemble $\sigma_a=|u_a\rangle\langle u_a|$, the corresponding output is $p_a|u_a\rangle\langle u_a|$. A zero weight has $E_a=0$. The statement is a finite-dimensional operator identity and assumes no measurement postulate or outcome law.

items.title: The set of density operators is convex
items.statement: For a nonzero finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space $H$, the set of density operators on $H$ is convex: if $\rho,\sigma$ are density operators and $t\in[0,1]$, then $t\rho+(1-t)\sigma$ is a density operator.

items.title: The least purification environment dimension is the density rank
items.statement: For a density operator $\rho$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space $H$, the least possible dimension of a finite auxiliary space $K$ for which $\rho$ has a purification in $H\otimes K$ is $\operatorname{rank}(\rho)$.

title: Pure and Mixed States, Ensembles, and Schmidt Decomposition — Examples

items.title: Bell-state Schmidt decomposition and reduced density
items.statement: For $H=K=\mathbb C^2$ with ordered standard bases $e_0,e_1$, the Bell vector $\Psi=(e_0\otimes e_0+e_1\otimes e_1)/\sqrt2$ is already in Schmidt form: it is a finite sum $\sum_j s_j u_j\otimes v_j$ with positive coefficients and orthonormal families in both factors, here $s_0=s_1=1/\sqrt2$ and $u_j=v_j=e_j$. Its reduced state on either factor is $I_2/2$.
